end.summary:
Vihaan practised the structure of India’s courts and the idea of appeal.
They identified property-boundary disputes as civil cases and theft as a criminal case.
They explained that criminal cases concern law-breaking and society, not only the victim’s loss.
Vihaan requested a visual court hierarchy with arrows and began placing District Court first.
end.parentNote: Vihaan practised sorting civil and criminal cases and explaining why theft is treated as a crime against society. They also worked through District Court, High Court, and Supreme Court in order, using a visual diagram to clarify appeals. They briefly mixed up which side theft belonged on, then corrected it later by identifying it as criminal. At home, ask them to draw the three-court ladder and add an appeal arrow from District Court to High Court to Supreme Court.
